title: Browser/MCP/Relay source ledger
scope: Public primary-source research only; authorized independent fixtures, no policy-bypass route.

method.firecrawl_feedback: one partial-quality scrape feedback submitted successfully
method.github: Pinned commits, licenses, selected implementation and test excerpts fetched read-only
method.coverage: 10 projects/services; 9 project repository refs plus a separate Playwright core test ref. Search slots are not read/validated source counts.

failures.resolution: Found current platform/browser/long-sessions/keep-alive documentation by targeted search.

projects.name: OMP Browser Relay
projects.priority: highest: inspect existing installation; offline evidence contract first
projects.local_session: Existing Chrome via extension/native messaging; separate owned/borrowed tabs; no browser access performed.
projects.observation: observe/ariaSnapshot, screenshot/diffScreenshot; stale handles must be reacquired after navigation or worker recovery.
projects.concurrency: One active run per named tab; caller ownership and acquisition leases; ordinary child agents skip relay defaults, sidebar relay-only is a documented exception.
projects.recovery: Reattach does not replay possibly delivered input; worker replacement invalidates handles. Documentation/source disagree about extension ID installation details.
projects.reuse: Re-use existing dispatcher and browser receipt semantics; inspect busy-tab, open-lease, tab-isolation regression patterns; no new relay daemon.
projects.boundary: Read-only source research. No use on any host-refused origin; no install/sync/profile mutation; loopback is not a principal boundary.

projects.name: browser-use
projects.priority: migration-aware reference; do not import full agent loop
projects.local_session: 1.0 Browser() defaults to cloud; fresh local Chromium must be explicit. Current docs also describe user-browser attachment, not exercised.
projects.observation: Persistent Python REPL + browser-harness/raw CDP; screenshots on demand; old DOM watchdog excerpt belongs to pre-1.0 architecture.
projects.concurrency: No evidence here establishes safe concurrent input to one tab; separate browser/session ownership is required by our design.
projects.recovery: run() can return status=error; success is model verdict, done is only run completion. AgentHistoryList old replay/step interfaces removed.
projects.reuse: Result.error/status/partial distinction and compatibility checklist; omit second autonomous agent loop.
projects.boundary: No API/model/browser invocation; do not silently adopt cloud defaults.

projects.name: Stagehand
projects.local_session: localBrowser launch/connect or Browserbase browser handles; browser remains caller-owned.
projects.observation: observe returns selectors/actions, act executes instructions or observed actions, extract schema-validates data; direct observed actions are replayed by selector.
projects.concurrency: One Stagehand per handle according to v4 docs; no proof of conflict-free simultaneous writers on a tab.
projects.recovery: Cache hit avoids inference, not action execution; a cached selector is not an idempotency receipt.
projects.reuse: Separate observe/act/extract, scoped observation and typed extraction; dependency optional for later local fixture.
projects.boundary: Do not mix v3 ctor/env examples with v4 create/browser API; no model or Browserbase calls.

projects.name: Browserbase managed browser
projects.license: Hosted service terms; not covered by Stagehand MIT license
projects.priority: later optional remote fixture, not local desktop control
projects.local_session: Remote browser sessions and saved contexts, not this computer's Chrome.
projects.observation: Per-tab video replay documented; replay is historical and not proof of current frame.
projects.concurrency: Managed sessions available separately; multiple connections to one keepAlive session are not a single-writer protocol.
projects.recovery: keepAlive survives disconnect but respects timeout; explicit release needed; final statuses differ by session lifetime mode.
projects.reuse: Separate session lifecycle, context persistence and replay metadata; no new paid dependency this wave.
projects.boundary: No account/service invocation or purchase; replay signed URLs/API keys never public artifacts.

projects.name: Browser MCP
projects.version: main commit pinned; package version not selected
projects.priority: ownership/reconnect test patterns; not another service now
projects.local_session: Extension + one per-user daemon, separate slots for browser profiles.
projects.observation: Playwright-backed text/screenshot operations with hidden-tab checks.
projects.concurrency: Up to eight browser slots documented; per-browser IDs, pairing and Stop. Not evidence that shared cookies or same-tab concurrent writes are isolated.
projects.recovery: Reconnection grace, expiry of timed-out waiters, retirement of reused tab IDs; representative backend tests inspected.
projects.reuse: FakeExtension/FakeChromium, loopback fixture, identity-retirement tests; component reuse must retain notices and separately review file authority.
projects.boundary: README explicitly allows broad user-level file access; loopback/extension pairing does not make prompt injection harmless. No daemon installed.

projects.name: Agent Relay (AgentWorkforce)
projects.local_session: Agent process messaging/lifecycle coordination; not a browser executor and not OMP Browser Relay.
projects.observation: No browser DOM/screenshot capability established by SDK itself.
projects.concurrency: Agent identity, durable channels, delivery modes and typed actions; existing runtime owns execution.
projects.recovery: accepted/delivered/deferred/failed receipts; action invocation acknowledgement distinct from eventual completed/failed event; idempotency keys for messages, not proof of browser exactly-once.
projects.reuse: Result envelope vocabulary and explicit deferred deadline semantics; reuse existing origin-dispatch instead of adding broker.
projects.boundary: Do not execute relay init or send external messages; public name similarity does not establish relation to local OMP.
